You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: How many days after an onboarding issue remains open will the employment bot automatically close it?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): 60 days

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Onboarding > TaNewKi Welcome Call > Managers of New Team Members > Compliance]
The Senior People Operations Specialist completes a monthly audit of all open onboarding issues to ensure that the new team member, manager and People Operations team tasks are completed. More importantly, there are certain tasks which need to be completed in line with our company compliance (security, payroll, etc).

If any tasks are still outstanding, the People Operations Specialist will ping the relevant members on the issue requesting action on the items or checking whether the issue can be closed.

*It remains the responsibility of the People Operations Specialist to close the issue and remain compliant.*

The employment bot will automatically close any onboarding issues still open after 60 days.

[GitLab Offboarding > Offboarding Overview > Involuntary Terminations > Last Working Day]
[People Engineering automations](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/peopleops-eng/employment-automation) will generate the offboarding issue at the end of the team member's last working day, as per notification from the Team Member Relations Specialist (TMR) and the People Business Partner (PBP). Once the `Last Working Day` or Garden leave expires the team member will be officially offboarded from GitLab.  Prior to the offboarding issue and the overall process for the term listed below.

[GitLab Offboarding > Offboarding Overview > Involuntary Terminations > Offboarding Compliance]
The People Operations member in the relevant rotation will complete a weekly audit of all offboarding issues opened within that specific week and check that all People Operations tasks have been completed and that the label `peopleops::done` has been added.

All offboarding tasks by all Departments need to be completed within 5 days of the offboarding date. For systems that are more critical and time sensitive, these will be completed within the first 24 hours (example 1Password, Slack) by the relevant Departments. Information about application & system deprovisioners can be found on the [Tech Stack Applications handbook page](/handbook/business-technology/tech-stack-applications/).

To ensure a successful completion of the offboarding issue, it is important that all tasks are checked off, whether the system/tool is applicable to the offboarding team member or not. Checking the box indicates one of the following:

- I have revoked team member access to this particular system/tool
- I have checked and this team member was not given access to this particular the system/tool.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
60 days
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
